title: Compliance scope and log retention workshop - PineRiver Trust
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-22
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sanjay Rao (CISO - PineRiver), Elena Torres (Head Eng), Maya Klein (Compliance), Tom Beck (Platform)
summary: Discovery focused on data residency, GDPR scope, HIPAA applicability, log retention policies, and what of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private would map to PineRiver Trust's controls. Actionable asks: send SOC2 + HIPAA addendum, architecture diagram for private VPC deployment, sample logging/retention config. SE to run a short KV-cache/latency benchmark if they decide dedicated pilot.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Alex (AE) - Email SOC 2 report and HIPAA addendum to Maya by 2025-09-24
Priya (SE) - Prepare architecture diagram for Private VPC + BYOK flow and share with Tom and Elena by 2025-09-26
Tom (Platform) - Provide current log retention policy and SIEM endpoints to Redwood by 2025-09-25
Maya (Compliance) - Send high-level list of regulatory controls required (PCI? GLBA? specific banking regs) by 2025-09-24
next_steps: Schedule 60-min technical deep dive (dedicated/private deployment) w/ infra team (proposed: 2025-09-29)
SE to run latency/cost estimate for a 24/7 dedicated pool sized for 50 req/s
AE to follow up with pricing tiers and pilot terms for 3-month dedicated eval
body_transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Alex AE on Redwood, Priya is our SE and will cover the technical pieces.
[00:14] Sanjay Rao: Hi all, Sanjay here. We're trying to understand how Redwood fits into our data residency and compliance requirements, especially for downstream logs and PII.
[00:27] Elena Torres: We want clarity on whether hosted is doable or if we need dedicated/private given our custodial responsibilities.
[00:35] Priya Raman: Totally — we'll walk through options. Quick question: is PineRiver treating LLM requests as PHI/PCI data or more like enriched metadata?
[00:44] Maya Klein: Good question — for customer financials we treat certain fields as sensitive; HIPAA isn't primary, but GDPR and GLBA-ish financial regs are in play. For one business line HIPAA may trigger (health savings accounts).
[01:02] Alex Morales: Understood. So primary drivers are GDPR data residency, GLBA/financial controls, and some lines with HIPAA. We'll map controls to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[01:18] Tom Beck: Also we have strict logging rules — logs must be retained for 7 years for audit, but with PII redaction allowed for some logs. We also can't forward raw prompts to third-party SIEMs that include full PII unless anonymized.
[01:32] Priya Raman: Makes sense. High level: Hosted has the fastest path but logs and prompts may be accessible to our platform for debugging (we have controls to limit that). Dedicated gives you isolated capacity; Private (VPC/on-prem) is where you get full control and can keep everything in your network.
[01:50] Elena Torres: Can you describe the encryption and key flow for Private? BYOK? HSM?
[01:56] Priya Raman: For Private we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with KMS integrations. We also have HSM-backed key storage options for enterprise. The runtime can be configured to encrypt KV cache at rest and use TLS in transit. For Hosted we offer encrypted at rest and in transit, and optional BYOK for specific enterprise tiers.
[02:16] Sanjay Rao: And audit logs? We need immutable audit trails for any admin actions and model version rollouts. Can we export those to our Splunk/Elastic?
[02:28] Alex Morales: Yes, the Console exports audit logs; you can stream to S3 or syslog endpoints — we can forward to Splunk/Elastic via your collectors. For Private it's direct within your VPC.
[02:40] [crosstalk] Maya Klein: What's the default retention on logs in Hosted?
[02:45] Priya Raman: Defaults are 90 days in Hosted Console, but you can purchase extended retention add-ons for 1/3/7 years depending on plan. For Dedicated you can set retention per-route; Private you control retention fully. 
[03:02] Tom Beck: So for our 7-year audit requirement Hosted won't work unless we buy extended retention and ensure logs are stored in our region — is that correct?
[03:11] Priya Raman: Correct. And region placement matters for GDPR. Hosted supports EU-region tenancy for EU-hosted models and logs — but there are cross-region fallbacks in rare outages unless you pin model placements.
[03:25] Elena Torres: How do you handle redaction or PII scrubbing in logs? We can't keep full prompts with SSNs.
[03:33] Priya Raman: We offer configurable redaction filters and an automated PII detection pipeline. Usually you set filters at the SDK/edge to redact before sending or at the service side using regex and ML detectors. For strict controls we recommend edge-side redaction + private deployment.
[03:51] Sanjay Rao: We need to understand data flow for a user request: mobile app -> backend -> Redwood API. Where might persistent data live?
[03:59] Alex Morales: Good callout. Typical flow: your backend calls Redwood API. By default transient request metadata and tokens are stored briefly for debugging and telemetry; persistent artifacts are logs, traces, and optionally cached KV entries if you enable prefix caching for performance. In Private, those caches and logs live in your VPC/storage.
[04:22] [00:04:22] Maya Klein: Can you provide examples of what "transient" means? How long are prompts kept?
[04:29] Priya Raman: On Hosted default is 30 days for request transcripts unless you opt into deletion or extended retention controls. We also have a 'no-retain' mode for certain enterprise agreements where we don't persist prompts beyond immediate processing.
[04:40] Elena Torres: If we run a pilot, will dedicated also default to 30 days?
[04:45] Priya Raman: Dedicated gives you more control in the Console — you can set retention to 0/30/90/365 etc, or ship logs directly to your S3 with lifecycle policies.
[04:56] Tom Beck: For our compliance, we need to ensure logs are immutable and tamper-evident for audits. How's immutability enforced?
[05:04] Priya Raman: If you stream logs to S3 you can use object lock to enforce immutability. For Private, you control the storage layer and can enforce WORM policies.
[05:15] [00:05:15] Sanjay Rao: About GDPR — we need to ensure right-to-be-forgotten can be honored. If a prompt includes a customer's personal data, and they request deletion, is Redwood able to find and purge all copies (including caches and logs)?
[05:29] Alex Morales: We provide deletion workflows. For Hosted, deletion requests can be applied to primary logs and prompts, and we currently also support KV cache eviction for pinned keys. However if you require guaranteed deletion across backups you should look at Private deployment or Dedicated with BYOK and strict retention policies. We'll share our data deletion playbook.
[05:50] Maya Klein: Also do you support pseudonymization so we can keep audit trails without raw PII?
[05:57] Priya Raman: Yes, pseudonymization via hashing or tokenization is common. We can show patterns for de-identification in the SDK. For high-assurance usecases we recommend that transformation happen on your side before calls.
[06:09] Elena Torres: Any certifications — SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA BAA — available? We need SOC 2 Type II and a HIPAA addendum for that line of business.
[06:20] Alex Morales: We are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO reports in progress. We do sign HIPAA BAAs for customers with covered needs — we have an addendum that Priya can share.
[06:31] [00:06:31] Sanjay Rao: Can we see pen test reports or any third-party attestation?
[06:36] Alex Morales: Yes, we'll include summary pen-test info in the package. For detailed reports we'll need an NDA/secure link; we'll coordinate through AE.
[06:45] Tom Beck: Is there an option to run inference within our VPC so that telemetry never leaves our network?
[06:52] Priya Raman: That's the Private deployment option — control plane can still be customer-managed; compute runs in your VPC or on-prem. That ensures telemetry and logs never cross Redwood's network.
[07:02] Maya Klein: If we pick Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs but isolated), who sees the logs? Is there any human access from Redwood support?
[07:10] Priya Raman: Dedicated nodes are logically isolated, but our support ops have emergency access with break-glass procedures that are audited. If you need zero human access, Private/on-prem is the right path.
[07:23] Elena Torres: Latency question — some of our products are user-facing with 90ms SLOs on text generation. How does Dedicated/Private compare?
[07:31] Priya Raman: For token generation small seqs, Dedicated in the same region can hit low 30-80ms depending on model. Private on-prem can get even lower but depends on your infra. We'll run benchmarks.
[07:43] [00:07:43] Sanjay Rao: Regarding logging restrictions: we can't store full prompts for more than 30 days in EU and must redact sensitive fields. Does Redwood support per-route masking rules?
[07:56] Alex Morales: Yes — per-route and per-model masking rules are supported in the Console or via API. You can apply JSON-path based redaction or custom ML filters.
[08:07] Maya Klein: On incident response — if there is a data leakage, what is Redwood's incident response timeline and commitments?
[08:15] Alex Morales: We have an incident response SLAs for Enterprise: acknowledge within 1 hour, full triage within 24-72 hours depending on severity, with forensic packet capture availability for Private. We'll share our IR playbook.
[08:30] Tom Beck: Do you provide role-based access controls so we can limit who within Redwood org can trigger rollouts?
[08:36] Priya Raman: Yes RBAC, SSO/SAML integration, and fine-grained permissions in Console; audit logs capture who did what and when.
[08:46] Elena Torres: Does Redwood maintain copies of model weights or fine-tuned artifacts we provide?
[08:52] Priya Raman: We store model artifacts if you upload them to our registry. For Private you can host your own registry. We can also support ephemeral loading if you prefer not to persist weights.
[09:02] Sanjay Rao: Licensing concerns — if we fine-tune on customer data, are we exposing them to any risk?
[09:08] Alex Morales: Fine-tuning is isolated per customer; but you should ensure the dataset is sanitized. We can run an eval to detect leakage.
[09:16] [00:09:16] Maya Klein: About backup retention for logs — backups often live in another account regionally; does Redwood replicate?
[09:24] Priya Raman: By default we have cross-region replication for availability, but for customers with residency needs we can disable replication or pin everything to the EU region.
[09:36] Elena Torres: On the legal side — we need contract language for data locality, breach notification, and right-to-erasure. Do you have standard clauses?
[09:45] Alex Morales: Yes, our enterprise contracts include data residency language and breach notification timelines; we'll include redlines for legal.
[09:52] Tom Beck: On monitoring — can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route token logs? We need to map costs to business units.
[09:59] Priya Raman: Console offers token-level cost breakdowns and per-route cost dashboards; you can export detailed CSVs to your cost reporting pipeline.
[10:08] Sanjay Rao: Let's talk about the 'no retain' mode — operationally what does that mean for debugging?
[10:14] Priya Raman: No-retain means we do not persist request or response transcripts beyond processing; this limits debugging and analytics. In that mode we keep metrics but not raw content.
[10:25] Maya Klein: If we enable no-retain on Hosted, can we still use caching for latency improvements?
[10:31] Priya Raman: Cache typically requires persistent storage; no-retain is incompatible with persistent KV caching. You'd need Private or dedicated where you control caching storage.
[10:41] [00:10:41] Elena Torres: For the GDPR mapping, we need to know which processing activities count as "controller" vs "processor". What's Redwood's posture?
[10:50] Alex Morales: We are a processor by default when you call our API; you remain the controller. For Private deployments where you host everything in your VPC, you're effectively both. We'll provide a DPA draft.
[11:02] Tom Beck: Are there throttles or rate limits that could force fallback to another region? We need to avoid cross-border fallbacks for EU traffic.
[11:08] Priya Raman: You can pin region and set routing policies to avoid cross-region fallback. There are capacity-driven fallbacks but you can prefer strict placement to failover instead of routing cross-region.
[11:21] Sanjay Rao: Can we get a sample of the audit log format? We want to ingest into our SIEM and parse fields.
[11:28] Alex Morales: We'll share a sample JSON schema and a Splunk/Elastic ingest script.
[11:33] [00:11:33] Maya Klein: A quick question — do you offer indemnities for data breaches?
[11:38] Alex Morales: Standard infra indemnities are in our enterprise contracts; specific language can be discussed with legal.
[11:44] Elena Torres: Any constraints on private deployments around GPU HW vendors? We have an internal preference for A100s.
[11:51] Priya Raman: We support a range of hardware; for Private you can specify node types — A100/NVIDIA or AMD variants; we'll provide guidance on perf/cost tradeoffs.
[12:02] Tom Beck: For our pilot scope we want: EU region data residency, 90-day log retention for dev and 7-year for production, no human access to raw prompts for prod, and a BAA for the line with HIPAA. Feasible?
[12:17] Alex Morales: Feasible. Suggested path: start with Dedicated EU-only pilot with extended retention and BYOK, then migrate to Private for the strict prod needs (7-year retention and no human access). We'll map timelines and cost.
[12:34] Priya Raman: SE note: we should run a small latency benchmark with your payload to validate 90ms SLOs on chosen model. I'll need sample prompts and expected traffic pattern.
[12:45] Maya Klein: We'll prepare sample prompts with masked PII and a sanitized version.
[12:51] [00:12:51] Sanjay Rao: One more on HIPAA — if we sign a BAA, do you support sign-off for business associates across Dedicated?
[12:59] Alex Morales: Yes we sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer BAAs on enterprise tiers.
[13:08] Elena Torres: Competitors question: we looked at OpenAI's enterprise and AWS Bedrock. How do you differentiate on compliance?
[13:16] Alex Morales: We focus on production controls: pinning, dedicated pools, private VPCs, and clear logging/retention levers. Many platforms are flexible but our console exposes per-route security primitives and we provide audit tooling tailored for regulated shops.
[13:32] Tom Beck: Cost question — what are the delta costs for enabling BYOK + extended retention on dedicated?
[13:38] Priya Raman: We'll provide a cost estimate; generally BYOK is included at enterprise tiers, extended retention is an add-on (depends on volume), Dedicated has a baseline monthly reserve plus usage. AE will follow up with numbers.
[13:48] Maya Klein: For legal, we also need proof of encryption standards (AES-256, TLS 1.2/1.3).
[13:56] Alex Morales: We use TLS 1.2/1.3 and AES-256 at rest. HSM options meet FIPS certifications for key storage. We'll include a security spec doc link in the follow-up.
[14:08] [00:14:08] Elena Torres: Any limitations on redaction — regex won't catch complex PII patterns, how reliable are ML detectors?
[14:16] Priya Raman: ML detectors are strong but not perfect; best practice is to combine client-side filters + server-side detectors. We can ship a test harness to estimate recall/precision on your sample corpus.
[14:28] Sanjay Rao: SLA expectations — what uptime SLA do you offer for Dedicated? We need 99.95% for prod.
[14:35] Alex Morales: Dedicated SLAs are available at 99.95% for enterprise contracts with defined credits for downtime. Private SLAs depend on your infra.
[14:45] Tom Beck: Will Redwood sign SOC 2 related access constraints?
[14:49] Alex Morales: Our SOC 2 report covers operational controls and we can provide complementary attestations and specific access control clauses in contracts.
[14:58] Maya Klein: About forensics — do you capture request IDs we can correlate to app logs?
[15:03] Priya Raman: Yes we expose request IDs and trace context so you can correlate with your logs.
[15:09] [00:15:09] Elena Torres: Ok can we recap the recommended path and immediate deliverables?
[15:14] Alex Morales: Recommended: 1) Run a Dedicated EU pilot with 3-month term, extended retention for prod route (7 years), BYOK, and canary to Private if needed. 2) SE-run latency/cost benchmark using your sample prompts. 3) Legal/Compliance receive SOC2/HIPAA/IR playbook. 4) Schedule technical deep dive.
[15:35] Sanjay Rao: Sounds good. We'll need the contract redlines around breach notification and data residency.
[15:42] Alex Morales: We'll include those in the follow-up.
[15:46] [00:15:46] Priya Raman: I'll note the technical items: architecture diagram for Private VPC, sample audit log schema, and the benchmark plan.
[15:55] Maya Klein: Also include a clear data deletion playbook for GDPR compliance.
[16:00] Alex Morales: Absolutely. We'll send the list and owners after the call. Thanks everyone.
[16:05] [crosstalk/closing] Meeting ended at 15:47 UTC
notes: References: security packet link (shared in follow-up), sample audit-log schema, DPA/DPA draft. Customer emphasized EU residency, GLBA/financial controls, occasional HIPAA requirement.
